response.sql:
WITH media_type_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    mt.MediaTypeId,
    CAST(SUM(t.Bytes) AS DECIMAL(38,10)) / SUM(t.Milliseconds) as byte_rate,
    COUNT(t.TrackId) as track_count
  FROM MediaType mt
  JOIN Track t ON mt.MediaTypeId = t.MediaTypeId
  GROUP BY mt.MediaTypeId
),
overall_avg_rate AS (
  SELECT AVG(byte_rate) as overall_avg 
  FROM media_type_stats
),
filtered_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    mts.byte_rate, 
    mts.track_count,
    mts.byte_rate - oar.overall_avg as excess
  FROM media_type_stats mts
  CROSS JOIN overall_avg_rate oar
  WHERE mts.byte_rate > oar.overall_avg
)
SELECT 
  AVG(byte_rate) as avg_rate,
  AVG(track_count) as avg_track_count,
  AVG(excess) as avg_excess
FROM filtered_stats

assumptions.assumption: Byte rate is computed as total bytes divided by total milliseconds per media type; the result is a decimal with preserved precision using DECIMAL(38,10) to satisfy 'without rounding'.
Media types are uniquely identified by MediaTypeId. Grouping by MediaTypeId ensures correct aggregation even if media type names are not unique in the schema.
All tracks in Track have MediaTypeId NOT NULL (enforced by schema), so 'using only tracks linked to a media type' is automatically satisfied by the JOIN.

alternatives.interpretation: If 'grouped by name' literally means GROUP BY the Name column (assuming or requiring names to be unique), group directly by mt.Name instead of mt.MediaTypeId.
